title: Banana and Walnut Tarte Tatin with Brown Sugar
changes_from_base: Bananas and toasted walnuts in place of apples, set in a quick butter and brown sugar sauce that needs only 5 min on the hob.
summary: Classic Tatin made quicker with bananas and toasted walnuts in a buttery brown sugar sauce.
equipment: 23 cm ovenproof heavy frying pan or Tatin tin

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the pastry
steps.text: whizz or rub the flour, icing sugar, salt and butter to crumbs, add the egg and bring it together. Wrap the disc and chill 30 min.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan). Dry-fry the walnuts in the pan over medium heat, stirring, for about 2 min until fragrant, then tip onto a plate.

steps.title: Brown sugar base
steps.text: melt the butter in the same pan, stir in the brown sugar and salt until smooth and bubbling, then take it off the heat and scatter the walnuts over.

steps.title: Bananas
steps.text: peel them, halve lengthwise, then cut each half in two. Lay them rounded side down in snug circles on the nuts. Ripe but firm bananas, still a little green at the stem, hold together best.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: return the pan to medium heat for 5 min, until the sauce bubbles up round the fruit.

steps.title: Top and bake
steps.text: roll the pastry 2 cm wider than the pan, drape it over and tuck in the edge. Bake 25-30 min until golden, then leave 10 min.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: loosen the edge with the knife, cover with the plate and, using tea towels, turn it over in one go. Serve warm, with vanilla ice cream if you like. Any sauce left in the pan can be spooned back over the top.

tips: Very ripe, spotty bananas turn to mush, so save those for banana bread.
Toast the walnuts only until they smell nutty; they keep cooking in the oven.
Cut the bananas just before using so they do not darken.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best eaten warm on the day; bananas darken as they stand. Cover and chill leftovers for up to 1 day.
